title: Night GPU ops — tactician journal
content:
Night shift scratchpad — quick brain dump and checklist

Context / goals for tonight:
- Keep 6 prod pools at >= 95% healthy (gpu: a100-p4 xnn clusters).
- Run planned drain on pool-alpha (node rotation) and ensure fallback routing to pool-beta.
- Validate KV cache warmup strategy after rolling restart; avoid epoch drop in latency SLO.

Immediate checks (first 15m):
- [ ] check cluster health: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=pool-alpha -o wide`
- [ ] query pool metrics: `promql:sum by(pool)(up{job=nv-gpu-exporter})`
- [ ] open SLO dashboard (console -> per-route latency) and note p50/p95 baseline

Quick commands to keep handy:
- drain node gracefully: `kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
- snapshot KV cache hit rate: `curl -s http://metrics.local/cache/hit_rate?pool=pool-alpha`
- warmup script (local): `./scripts/prefetch_kv.sh --pool pool-alpha --prompts sample-prompts/warmup-set.jsonl`

Planned sequence for pool-alpha rotation (risk: transient increase in tail-latency):
1) pick node-17 (least pods) at 01:10 UTC; cordon + drain after confirming replicas in pool-beta.
2) monitor autoscaler behavior — expect +2 pods in pool-beta within 3m. If not, abort and rollback.
3) run warmup script against pool-alpha once node is back up and model server healthy.
4) measure KV hit-rate and p95 for 10m windows; if p95 > baseline+150ms, escalate.

Escalation plan (fast):
- p95 > baseline + 300ms for >5m: flip routing policy to prefer pool-beta (console -> routes -> prefer: pool-beta) and open a high-sev incident in #infra-ops.
- Request immediate extra capacity: ping Amit (pager) to spin an emergency node in pool-gamma.

Notes / gotchas from last run:
- last rotation (2024-10-30) showed a KV cache cold-start that kept p95 elevated for ~14m; cause was incomplete warmup script (missing quantized-8bit path). Added `--quant-path q8` flag in warmup script.
- metric `gpu_temp_over_85` sometimes fires due to bad thermals in rack-3b; check bmc logs before scheduling heavy batch runs.

Temporary TODOs (personal):
- [ ] update scripts/prefetch_kv.sh to detect model variant and call compatible warmup set (q4/q8/fp16). (30m)
- [ ] open PR with small logging improvements in serving-runtime to annotate warmup origin (PR draft created: /pull/981). (20m)
- [ ] write short runbook snippet for weekend on-call redirecting routing when pool-alpha drains unexpectedly. (15m)

Edge-network / routing checks:
- confirm egress rules to region-us-west are intact after firewall rule change (ticket INFRA-2147).
- run `curl -I https://status.redwood-inference.com/healthz` from a node in pool-alpha to ensure external reachability.

Small experiments to try if capacity allows (low priority):
- try batching tweak: reduce max-batch-delay from 10ms -> 6ms for low-latency routes and measure cost delta overnight. (safe rollback: 2h)
- test fallback model variant (smaller quantized variant) on 1% traffic using canary route. Ensure consistency checks for hallucination rate recorded.

Notes-to-self / mental model:
- Always assume KV cache cold-start is the single largest driver of p95 spikes during node rotation. Warmup early and prefer small parallel prefetch jobs rather than a single long-run prefetch.
- Keep an eye on autoscaler thrashing: if scale up then down within 5m repeatedly, probably the probe timings need smoothing.

Incident snippets (for timeline if needed):
- 01:12 UTC — cordon node-17 (planned).
- 01:17 UTC — drain started; pods shift to pool-beta (observed +3 pods).
- 01:22 UTC — first warmup run launched; KV hit-rate initial 0.02 -> 0.52 in 8m.
- 01:40 UTC — p95 back to baseline. Close loop.

Open questions / decide later:
- Is it worth pre-warming a small persistent cache replica in each pool to provide fast first-bite hits? Pros: lower tail latency during rotation. Cons: cost, complexity.
- Should warmup script be part of node-init or run as a daemonset job post-join? (current thought: daemonset job triggered once health checks pass)

Random micro-notes: 
- coffee ready at 00:55 — bring small thermos.
- remind product about canary windows: shorten to 10m for model-variant tests to speed failures detection.

If I get blocked:
- DM Amit with `@Amit` and summary + screenshot of latency panel, logs (pod logs) and exact command I ran.
- If cluster is unstable, mark `on-call-run` in Ops doc and handoff to morning SRE.

End of shift checklist (before handoff):
- [ ] confirm all drained nodes rejoin and uncordoned if needed
- [ ] paste snapshot of p50/p95 + KV hit-rate into #shift-handoffs with short notes
- [ ] push small changelist for warmup script improvements

— R.P.

(keep this file ephemeral; once runbook gets cleaned up, move to shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/runbooks/night-rotations)
